rubrics.criterion: The interior (middle) route-step construction in BOTH the v7 and v6 OSRM-compatible APIs lives in a single well-scoped step-conversion function that the leg-assembly code calls, rather than the whole banner/mapping/bearing pipeline being pasted into a per-step closure in each generation; an equivalent re-scoped helper that owns the step-build work for one maneuver triple is acceptable, but the per-triple closure no longer restates the pipeline itself.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the six injected sites are the same route-translation absorption split across the two API generations, and a repair that only restores one generation leaves the other service emitting duplicated construction; this rubric forces both generations to be addressed.

rubrics.criterion: The v7 transit-plan step loop delegates each step's guidance (relative-direction instruction, post-transition text, street-name handling, bearings, and distance-proportional duration) to a single per-step owner - the maneuver constructor the file already defines, or an equivalent re-scoped helper - instead of building the whole step inline at the loop, and the instruction/duration helpers it relies on live in one place rather than being re-derived at the loop site.
rubrics.rationale: This is the deepest injected chain (depth 3) and the turn-by-turn heart of the plan API; leaving the loop with the expanded block in place is the signature failure mode for this case.

rubrics.criterion: The GTFS credential-verification routine downloads through a shared authenticated-request/download path (the same one that backs feed measurement, or an equivalent single owner of that machinery) instead of its own inline request chain, so the request/send/status/bytes logic has one implementation in the file rather than two.
rubrics.rationale: verify_feed absorbed fetch_feed; restoring a single owner of the download is the central repair for this module, and any repair that keeps two inline request chains fails it.

rubrics.criterion: The OTP router-config render resolves each realtime feed's credential and names each stream's updater through module-level (or comparably scoped) helpers rather than pasting the credential resolution and the stream-kind -> updater-name matching inline into the zone loop.
rubrics.rationale: for_zone absorbed two free functions (credential and otp_updater); this completer holds the render pass to single-sourcing both pieces of zone policy.

rubrics.criterion: Feed-summary row assembly for the bbox listing shares a single implementation owner (the existing summarizer the by-id endpoint already uses, or a re-scoped helper used by both the bbox and by-id endpoints) instead of two copies, one inline at the request handler and one in the shared function.
rubrics.rationale: list_feeds absorbed summarize while leaving summarize live for feeds_by_id; the repair must close that duplication in a way that keeps a single row-assembly implementation across both endpoints.

rubrics.criterion: Across all the touched files, no function in the route, plan, feed-verification, config-render, or listing paths retains a long duplicated construction sequence that restates another same-file function's implementation, including any switched-to-inline closures or block expressions that were introduced solely to hold the pasted body.
rubrics.rationale: Resolution at the named sites is necessary but not sufficient; a partial repair that relocates the paste into a different inline form would leave the structural duplication intact elsewhere.

rubrics.criterion: Glue introduced only to feed the pasted code - alias bindings of the call-site arguments (e.g. an Option<&T> rebinding, a `&`-reborrow of an enclosing parameter, a local rebinding of the credentials config) - is removed alongside the restoration of delegation, so no binding exists purely to make a copy compile at its new home.
rubrics.rationale: These aliases are diagnostic fingerprints of the paste-in; their persistence is evidence the inlining was merely reshaped, not undone.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merge the v6 and v7 OSRM-compatible APIs, wire one generation's types into the other, or otherwise unify the two generations' route-step conversion into one path - the two generations remain independent translations with their own distinct serialized output.
rubrics.rationale: A 'fix' for the cross-generation duplication that consolidates the two APIs into one would break the compatibility contract both generations exist to serve; this guards against an over-broad interpretation of 'remove the duplication'.

rubrics.criterion: No leftover of the inline form remains at the repaired sites: no comment claiming the inline construction is deliberate, no unused result-typed capture (such as a `_body` binding) left to justify the paste, and no now-orphaned-but-repasted helper whose body still matches an absorbed section.
rubrics.rationale: Stale inline-form markers and unused captures are the debris the injection leaves behind; a clean repair removes them rather than describing code that no longer exists.

rubrics.criterion: The OSRM route-step conversion in both generations still maps every internal ManeuverType variant to its paired OSRM maneuver type and direction (including transit, ferry, elevator, building, roundabout, ramp, fork, merge, and the destination/uturn variants); no mapping arm is dropped or collapsed in the extracted path.
rubrics.rationale: The injected step construction carries a large exhaustive match that is easy to lose an arm of during extraction; this is a concrete, behavior-visible regression specific to this route-translation pipeline.

rubrics.criterion: The v7 plan's spoken instruction set still covers every relative-direction form - the absolute-direction `Depart` form with its Walk/Bike/Drive/Transit mode selection and the bare `Depart.` fallback, sharp/slight/left/right turns, continue, roundabout, elevator, U-turn, and the EnterStation/ExitStation/FollowSigns `Continue.` form - and the `Continue for ...` post-transition instruction still appears only for non-zero distances.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed maneuver-instruction helper is a long direction-based match; a piecewise repair risks dropping or merging a spoken form, regressing the audible guidance customers hear.

rubrics.criterion: Per-step durations in the v7 plan are still apportioned from the leg's total duration by the step's distance share, using the leg's reported duration when present and the start/end elapsed-time fallback otherwise, and zero-length legs still yield a zero duration rather than dividing by zero.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed leg_duration_seconds helper encodes a reported-vs-elapsed precedence and a zero-guard; an extraction that changes the precedence or drops the guard regresses timing on OTP legs that don't report duration.

rubrics.criterion: The transit-zoner bbox response keeps its relevance-descending, feed-id-tiebreak ordering and the full per-feed field set (provider, url, authorization type and info url, realtime summaries, bbox corners, area, relevance), and the OTP router config still records skipped realtime feeds with their feed id and a credential-hint reason distinguishing 'missing credential' from 'cannot use'.
rubrics.rationale: Two concrete, behavior-visible outputs depend on the changed code paths: the bbox list ordering and the skipped-feed record shape; a refactor that reshuffles either regresses the page or OTP boot.

rubrics.criterion: The rendered OTP router-config still maps each published stream to its updater name and polling frequency (trip updates and vehicle positions at the faster interval, alerts at the slower one) and still applies the credential to the updater URL or headers per the stream's auth kind, with no stream dropped from the config.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed otp_updater and credential helpers encode per-stream intervals and auth application; losing a stream or its frequency regresses OTP routing for that feed.
